# Guard test: no proxy /slots without ?model= (AC3a)

**Parent:** LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 · **Slice:** 2 of 6 (test-first) · **Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

Land the static guard test that fails whenever any proxy code path constructs a `/slots` URL without a `?model=` component, seeded with an explicit allowlist naming the sites the audit found.

## Why this slice

AC3(a) must be a regression fence, not a one-off assertion: after slices 3–4 the allowlist is empty and any future model-less `/slots` construction fails the suite. Writing it before the fixes (test-first) makes each later slice provably close its own allowlist entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new test module statically scans `proxy/proxy/**/*.py` and asserts every `/slots` URL construction site carries a `?model=` component, either inline or via a documented appender.
- [ ] Offending sites are held in an explicit, documented allowlist so the test is green on landing — the allowlist contains exactly the sites the audit (slice 1) identified, each entry commented with the follow-up slice that removes it.
- [ ] A synthetic violation (a temporary `"/slots"` URL built without `?model=` in a scanned file) makes the test fail with the offending file:line and the reason in the assertion message.
- [ ] The test runs offline in under one second and passes through the test skill's changed-scope gate together with the existing `proxy/tests/test_slots_*` modules.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py`, using `ast` parsing plus a small URL-builder recogniser (pattern precedent: `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`).
- Recognise `f".../slots"`, `_build_llama_url(..., "/slots")` and literal `"/slots"` arguments; require a neighbouring `?model=` or a helper call known to append it.
- Keep an `ALLOWLIST` constant keyed by `(relative_path, symbol)`; assert no stale entries (an allowlisted site that no longer exists also fails, so the list cannot rot).
- Add a self-test for the "stale allowlist entry fails" rule so the fence itself is covered.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py` — the new guard test (new file)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — existing `?model=` appending builder the scan must accept
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_check_slot_availability` URL construction
- `proxy/proxy/backend_health.py` — `/slots` fallback probe
- `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py` — `_probe_gpu_wedge` probe URL
- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — `_probe_slot_capacity_sync` probe URL
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — AST source-scan test pattern to mirror

## Dependencies

- Depends on: LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12 (static audit inventory) — the allowlist must match the audited set

## Deliverables

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py` with a documented allowlist; green on landing, and the fence that later slices tighten.

# Goal

Document the new capacity-signal surface so the next operator (or agent)
reading `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` can read
the section, override the stale-rate target, and understand exactly how the
live-work derivation pairs with `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
without reading the code.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC5). Depends on the two
implementation slices — document the surface **as built**, not as planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5.1 (documentation).** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and
  `REFERENCE.md` describe the `## Local capacity signals` section: which
  figures it carries (poll count, `slots_stale` count/rate, `capacity_hint`
  counts and shares, saturated-without-live-work count and shares), when it is
  omitted, and where it is rendered in `report.md`.
- **AC5.2 (JSON keys documented).** `REFERENCE.md` documents the additive
  `capacity_signals` keys (`slots_stale`, `capacity_hint`,
  `saturated_without_live_work`, `targets`) with their field meanings, and
  states that the pre-existing `status_capacity_hint` /
  `denial_attribution.capacity_hint` keys are unchanged.
- **AC5.3 (target documented).** The `--stale-rate-target` flag is documented
  with its `0.05` default, how an override flows into both the Markdown and the
  JSON, and how to set it on the 05:00 cron line — with a copy-pasteable
  example.
- **AC5.4 (derivation documented consistently).** The docs describe the
  schema-2/schema-3 live-work derivation and the stale-rate denominator
  (polls without a `slots_stale` field excluded, never counted as fresh) in
  wording consistent with the `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  docstring and the shared `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` module — no
  contradictory description of the same rule.
- **AC5.5 (caveats retained).** The docs keep the caveat that the stale rate is

  and note the retained-log coverage limitation.
- **AC5.6 (cron unchanged).** The docs state that the nightly pipeline gained no
  network call, LLM call or interactive prompt, and that an empty window

## Minimal implementation

  section).
- Cross-link the two documents to

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`

## Risks

## Deliverables

Updated `SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` with section, keys, flag/override, cron
example, derivation rule and caveats.

Redefine `remote-ok` to *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: it keeps the local route and never waits for a slot (parent AC15, AC16, AC20). This child lands **before** the default inversion so the suite stays green - today `remote-ok` is a non-default value, so changing its meaning breaks no headerless caller.

## Goal

Make the value that will become the default safe to be the default: it attempts local when a slot is free, and steps straight to the next provider in the chain when local cannot serve the request right now - no queue entry, no deferral, no local-capacity `429`.

## Scope

- `apply_local_preference()` loses `strip_by_preference`; the capacity strip (`CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`) and its remote-less carve-out are kept byte-identical, so no preference can empty a chain.
- Remove (or neutralise) both dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: ... "providers": []` branches in the two dispatch cycles.
- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` declines to enqueue for `remote-ok`, returning the `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent outcome so the caller falls through immediately.
- Docstrings for `apply_local_preference`, `local_preference_for_request` and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` state the new meaning and the historic-name warning.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: the preference-table row for `remote-ok` and the per-exit fall-through notes that describe the strip are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone (no preference-based strip exists any more).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (no preference strip: `remote-ok` keeps the local route, parent AC15).** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the only preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as a headerless request attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (the upstream calls include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces no `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC3 (no preference can empty a chain, parent AC16).** The `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` is served locally (200, zero remote calls); the `private` model + absent header is unchanged at this stage; a normal chain with local down serves from the next remote entry, and exhaustion only when nothing is left to try. The two dead empty-chain branches are gone (grep-asserted). **Restates parent AC16:** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11445`, `:12142` as of 2026-10-30). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC4 (immediate step, no queue, parent AC20).** For each local-exit cause enumerated in parent AC20 (slot saturated, prefill-ETA over budget, local cooldown, residency/thrash skip, lease held, per-entry context cap) a `remote-ok` request produces `X-Local-Route: remote`, a `contention_queue` wait of 0, and exactly one upstream call. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics.
- **AC5 (documentation matches, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` no longer states that `remote-ok` removes the local route, the historic-name warning is present, and the pinned exit-table docs test (`test_local_only_exit_docs.py`) passes with the re-anchored `too_large` rows.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the preference strip in `apply_local_preference()`; keep the capacity strip and carve-out untouched.
2. Delete the two `PREF_REMOTE_OK` empty-chain branches.

data.description:
Retire the deprecated `local-only` wire value with a **loud** `400` (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4): never a silent demotion to `local-preferred` and never a silent resolution to the default. This child also builds the retirement mechanism that the later `prefer-local` retirement reuses, so the two retirements share exactly one implementation.

## Goal

A client still sending `local-only` gets an attributable, actionable failure instead of a policy it did not ask for (silent demotion to a local-first default could bill a cost-capped client - the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson).

## Scope

- Remove the `local-only` entry from `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (and delete the alias table if nothing remains in it) and drop `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` from the live vocabulary.
- Extend the **single** parse/validation site (`admission_reserve.parse_preference()`) with a retired-value outcome carrying the retired value and its successor guidance; no second parser and no per-call-site comparison.
- Emit the `400` at the request entry point **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written; the body is stable (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only *chain*).
- Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection, carrying the retired value, the successor guidance and the session id when present.
- Scope guard (parent AC3): provider names, the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` reason token stay unchanged.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_preference_vocabulary_v2.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (loud rejection, parent AC1).** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` returns `400` with `code: local_preference_retired` and the successor guidance, emitted before routing: the fake transport records zero upstream calls, and no queue entry, lease or cooldown state is created. **Restates parent AC1:** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` is no longer normalised to `local-preferred`. It is rejected with `400` and a stable JSON body (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only chain rather than a preference value), emitted **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written (fake transport records zero upstream calls). It must **not** silently degrade to the active default (`remote-ok`, AC21): a silent demotion would let a cost-capped client be billed without consent — the exact 2026-10-25 defect (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG) — and would make the retirement unobservable.
- **AC2 (not silently demoted, parent AC1).** No code path maps `local-only` to `local-preferred` or to `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`; a test asserts the response is a rejection even when the local route is free and the request would otherwise succeed locally.
- **AC3 (attributable, parent AC2).** Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection naming the retired value, the successor and the session id when one is present; a test asserts a single line and its fields.
- **AC4 (vocabulary, parent AC4).** The alias table no longer contains `local-only` (asserted so the removal cannot silently regress); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep their exact pre-change parse results; an unknown value still falls back to the default. **Restates parent AC4:** `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"})` returns the retired outcome (a `local_preference_retired` rejection, never `local-preferred` and never the default); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep today's exact result; the absent header resolves to the new default `remote-ok` (AC21); one test asserts the alias table no longer contains `local-only` so the removal cannot silently regress.
- **AC5 (scope discipline, parent AC3).** Grep-asserted: the provider fixtures named `local-only`, the `local_only_refused` log prefix, the `_build_local_only_refusal*` builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` token are untouched. **Restates parent AC3:** Only `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary changes. Explicitly unchanged: a provider *named* `local-only` (test fixtures in `proxy/test_home_page.py`, the `private` model notes), the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`, `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, `_log_local_only_refusal`), and the canonical reason token `local_only_no_local_route`. Rationale: renaming them is churn that breaks log-grep consumers for no behavioural gain — recorded as a scope decision, not an oversight.
- **AC6 (documented, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` and the `config.yaml` commentary describe the retirement and the exact `400` shape with a migration note; the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph is removed.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the alias mapping and the live constant; keep `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` only as a retired-value registry entry naming its successors.
2. Add the retired outcome to `parse_preference()` and thread it through the request entry point (fail closed before dispatch).
3. Add the rejection warning and the stable body at the same place the other preference `400`s are built.
4. Update docs/config commentary and fill in the corresponding contract specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child.

data.description:
Bound `local-preferred` deferral at **three** consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, then let the request fall back to remote instead of emitting a fourth `429` (parent AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10). Reuses the existing retryability decision and the existing promotion shape - no third promotion path and no second classification.

## Goal

An unattended `local-preferred` worker currently spins on retryable `429`s for as long as the GPU stays contended (the 2026-10-25 incident shape). After three refusals it must get an answer from a paid tier, visibly, rather than nothing.

## Scope

- New bounded, TTL'd, per-session counter store (`proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py`, or an equivalent small dedicated module) keyed by the sanitised `X-Session-ID`; no unbounded growth, entry cap + TTL.
- Increment where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability; the counter never re-classifies a refusal.
- At the threshold, strip the local entry for that request using `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape and stamp `X-Local-Route: remote` + the new canonical token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` (registered in `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`).
- Additive refusal-body fields `deferral_refusals` and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third refusal), with every pre-existing field and header unchanged.
- Exactly one log line per escalation naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold.
- New config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`, `0` disables) documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing server-restart convention.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py` (new module for the bounded counter store)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_deferral_budget.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (bounded budget, parent AC5).** Refusals 1, 2 and 3 are unchanged in timing and shape (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`); the fourth request from the same session is **not** refused - the local entry is dropped for that request and the remote tier serves it.
- **AC2 (visible, never silent, parent AC6).** The escalation returns the upstream status with `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: deferral_refusals_exhausted`; exactly one log line names the session, count and threshold; the escalation is distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion in both header and log; no `Retry-After` is advertised on the terminal path.
- **AC3 (the refusal advertises its budget, parent AC7).** The body reports `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third), purely additive - pre-existing fields, headers and key order unchanged.
- **AC4 (lifecycle and bounded memory, parent AC8).** The counter resets on a successful local dispatch, on a non-retryable refusal or `too_large` promotion, on TTL expiry, and on `local_deferral_max_refusals` reconfiguration; the store is capped and TTL'd; a request with no resolvable session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. One test per reset trigger.
- **AC5 (one knob, parent AC10).** `local_deferral_max_refusals` is the only threshold source (default `3`); `0` restores unbounded deferral; documented as restart-required; no other default changes.
- **AC6 (no queue/lease leak, parent Constraints).** An escalated request never first enqueues and then dispatches remotely - the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted with the fake transport.
- **AC7 (cost-capped escape hatch, parent AC9).** A remote-less chain (`private`) keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating; the pin-local predicate and its five call sites agree on the escalation decision.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the counter store with TTL, cap and a reset API; unit-test it directly.
2. Hook the increment into the single retryability decision and the reset into the local-success / `too_large` / non-retryable paths.
3. Reuse the `too_large` promotion shape for the escalation and register the token in the single token table.
4. Add the two body fields in the single refusal builder and the escalation log line.
5. Add the config key and its commentary, then fill in the deferral-budget specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child. Independent of the vocabulary children (do not rebase its counter onto a preference comparison - use the existing pin predicate).

data.description:
# Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported saturated

Close the last 12 `saturated`-without-live-work polls by making the proxy
annotate the slot it is still draining: every abandonment records a matchable
identity (or an endpoint-wide entry), so a draining slot reads
`abandoned_busy` and only genuinely live work reports `saturated`.

## Problem statement

The AC1 fix (`LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK`) took `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` from **247 polls
(2.12 %)** to **12 polls (0.11 %)** over a comparable 11 h night, but not to
zero. Every remaining violation is a *draining* slot: llama-server has been
told to stop (the upstream stream was closed) yet has not freed the slot, and
nothing annotates it — `local_abandoned_slots=0`, so the poll reads
`saturated` even though nothing the proxy is waiting for occupies the pool.

The gap is therefore an **annotation** gap, not a liveness gap: the proxy
knows it abandoned the work, but the status builder cannot tie that
abandonment to the slot the backend is still draining.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether
  the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a draining ghost
  misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker).
  `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a ghost-driven
  `saturated` causes avoidable paid fallback.
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`.
  Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is
  as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when the pool holds only work the proxy abandoned, I
  want `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` (not `saturated`) so I can tell "busy
  because of us" from "busy because of live work".
- As the routing policy, I want a draining slot to never look saturated, so a
  needless cloud fallback is not triggered by work nobody is waiting for.
- As an analyst, I want each draining-slot abandonment attributable to a slot
  or to its endpoint, so a re-measured residual can be explained rather than
  merely counted.

## Evidence (from the AC4 run, preserved)

Re-measurement `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`, night 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30
07:00, artifacts in `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`
(`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, 12 rows, all fresh detail):

| episode | polls | attribution | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-30 06:57:36 | 3 (one second) | unattributable | `measured_cache_deficit` release 31 s earlier; `available_slots=0 total_slots=2 local_abandoned_slots=0`; pool idle again by 06:57:43 |
| 2026-10-30 06:01:20–21 | 2 | unattributable | — |
| 2026-10-29 20:19:25 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 295 s |
| 2026-10-29 20:35:03 | 1 | `prefill_deadline` | 14 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:36:23 | 2 | `no_progress_watchdog` | 182 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:47:30–31 | 2 | `prefill_deadline` | 48 s |
| 2026-10-30 01:43:11 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 520 s |

Two shapes of the same gap:

1. **Attributable (7 polls)** — an abandonment whose cancel succeeded leaves a
   slot that is still `is_processing` but carries **no** abandoned-registry
   entry (`local_abandoned_slots=0`), so the annotation does not fire.
2. **Unattributable (5 polls)** — a release with no slot identity at all
   (`measured_cache_deficit` on a record without a pinned slot), so the poll
   cannot be attributed even with the 600 s lookback.

Two further observations to confirm during implementation (not yet claimed as
causes):

- two rows (06:01:20, 01:43:11) report `available_slots=1` **alongside**
  `saturated`, which a purely-occupied pool cannot produce;
- one row reports `latency_ms=3355`, above the `/slots` detail budget, while
  `slots_detail_stale=false`.

If either turns out to be a distinct (non-lag) defect, record it as a
`discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` item rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it
   gave up on, or records an explicit "unknown slot, endpoint-wide" entry that
   the status builder can match to a processing slot on that endpoint (so a
   release without a slot id is still annotatable).
2. A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`
   until llama-server reports it free (registry TTL keeps it bounded; no
   leaked marker, no double decrement, no phantom lease).
3. `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`
   and never `idle`; a genuinely live, proxy-owned slot still reports
   `saturated` (the truthful-status contract of `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` is not
   weakened).
4. Deterministic tests (mocked `/slots` snapshot, injected clock) cover both
   shapes above, including the case where the draining slot is visible in a
   *fresh* snapshot, the endpoint-wide (unknown-slot) match, and the negative
   case (endpoint-wide entry present but the slot is owned by a live dispatch
   record → still `saturated`).
5. Re-measurement over a comparable night shows **0** `saturated`-without-live-
   work polls (baseline for this residual: 12 polls / 0.11 %, of which 5
   unattributable).
6. Full suite green through the `test` skill; docs updated where the
   abandonment → capacity interaction is described
   (`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Truthful status is not weakened** (`LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM`): an endpoint-wide
  match must never annotate a slot that a live dispatch record owns, and a
  fresh snapshot with genuinely live decode work must keep reporting
  `saturated`.
- The registry stays **in-process**, keyed by `(endpoint, slot)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s default), no
  timer task, no unbounded growth. An endpoint-wide entry needs a key that
  cannot collide with a real slot id.
- The annotation is **read-only status decoration**: it must never free or
  acquire capacity, double-decrement counters, or create a phantom lease.
- The status schema stays **additive** (`status_schema_version` 4:
  `abandoned*`, `local_abandoned_slots`, `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy`).
- **Measurement must remain possible.** `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  `_ABANDON_REASONS` currently excludes `measured_cache_deficit`, so that
  release is reported unattributable no matter how well the proxy annotates
  it — the set must be extended (with a test) or AC5 is unmeasurable.
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Existing state

- Registry: `_abandoned_slots` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), keyed
  `(endpoint_or_empty, slot_id)`; `_record_abandoned_slot` returns `None` when
  the slot id is not an `int`, so an unknown-slot abandonment is silently
  dropped — this is exactly the shape-2 gap.
- Matching: `_abandoned_slot_for(slot_id, endpoint=…)` tries the exact
  endpoint, then the legacy/default endpoint, then any endpoint carrying that
  slot id. There is no endpoint-wide (slot-less) match.
- Recording paths: `_release_unserved_dispatch` resolves the slot via
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup` *before* freeing the assignment (prefill deadline,
  client disconnect); session eviction resolves one slot per released record
  in `proxy/proxy/server.py`; the watchdog and orphan sweep record too.
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` passes **neither** slot id nor
  stream, which is the shape-2 source.
- Status builder: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` annotates `abandoned`,
  `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_at_seconds_ago`
  when the registry matches the slot id; `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0
  returns `abandoned_busy` when every generating slot is abandoned and keeps
  `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
- Residual behaviour: the 7 attributable polls reported
  `local_abandoned_slots=0` while a slot was `is_processing`, so the recorded
  identity did not match the draining slot (stale/mis-resolved id, or a slot
  the backend reassigned after the free) and the annotation never fired.
- Docs already describe the mechanism in
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (§ *Abandoned work*) and
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ *Abandoned local dispatches*).

## Desired change

1. Every abandonment path records either the slot it gave up on (resolved
   before the assignment is freed, and re-verified against the slot the
   backend actually reports) or an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry.
2. The status builder matches an endpoint-wide entry only to a processing slot
   on that endpoint that no live dispatch record owns, so the draining ghost is
   annotated and live work is not.
3. The annotation survives until llama-server reports the slot free (or the TTL
   elapses), and is dropped when the slot is observed free; re-abandoning
   refreshes it; no duplicate entries, no leak.
4. `capacity_hint` for a pool whose only work is draining stays
   `abandoned_busy` — never `saturated`, never `idle`.
5. `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` counts a `measured_cache_deficit`
   release as an abandonment event for attribution, with a test.
6. Docs updated where the abandonment → capacity interaction is described.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — abandoned-slot registry, release paths,
  endpoint-wide entry, slot re-verification.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status slot builder, endpoint-wide match,
  `compute_capacity_hint` (rule 0 unchanged in intent).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload
  (`local_abandoned_slots`).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — session-eviction slot resolution (if the recorded
  identity needs re-verification).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — registry, annotation and
  capacity-hint tests for both shapes.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — status payload contract.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — attribution set.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 7 attributable residuals are identity/matching failures,
  not TTL expiry — the longest release→poll gap observed is 520 s against a
  900 s TTL. Verify by logging the recorded slot id against the processing slot
  id during implementation.
- **Assumption:** AC5 (night re-measurement) is an operational run after
  deploy, mirroring the parent's child `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the plan step may
  decompose it into a follow-on child instead of blocking the code change.
- **Risk:** an endpoint-wide match annotates live work → weakens the truthful
  contract. Mitigation: require no live dispatch record for that slot, and
  cover the negative case with a deterministic test (AC4).
- **Risk:** a slot reported free and immediately reassigned could inherit a
  stale endpoint-wide entry. Mitigation: clear the entry on an observed free
  slot and keep the bounded TTL.
- **Risk (scope creep):** cooldown behaviour (`prefill_thrash_cooldown`) and
  the two anomalous rows (`available_slots=1`, 3.3 s latency) are **out of
  scope** here; record them as `discovered-from` items if confirmed.
- **Risk:** extending `_ABANDON_REASONS` changes the historical baseline
  (247 / 12 poll counts were computed with the narrower set). Mitigation: state
  the change in the report note and in the docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB` — parent: abandoned local dispatches leave
  llama-server busy (completed).
- `LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK` — AC1: abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel
  (completed; this item closes its residual).
- `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037` — AC4: re-measure one comparable night (completed;
  produced the 12-poll baseline).
- `LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2` — regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported
  saturated (completed).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — truthful-status contract (stale capacity hint
  reconciliation) that this item must not weaken.
- `LP-0MVT2KWF0000QTSM` — docs for abandoned-work status and cooldown scope
  (completed).
- Docs: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`,
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`; artifacts under
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is a producer interview needed before drafting, or does the seed context
  suffice?" — Answer (agent, from repo/worklog evidence): the seed context
  states the problem, the measured evidence, the target outcome, six testable
  ACs and the key files; no producer input is required to draft. Source:
  `wl show LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` (description authored by Map), evidence CSV in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent): the parent split re-measurement into its own child
  (`LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`), so the plan step should decompose AC5 the same way.
  **Open to producer override**, not blocking; recorded as an assumption above.
- Q: "Is `measured_cache_deficit` outside the abandonment reasons the
  verification script attributes?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes —
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` `_ABANDON_REASONS` lists only
  `prefill_deadline`, `session_evicted`, `no_progress_watchdog`,
  `client_disconnect`, while `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` exports
  `MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON`. Captured as constraint 5 / AC-relevant scope.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`?" — Answer (OPEN QUESTION, for implementation):
  not determinable from the artifacts alone (no recorded-slot-id field in the
  12-row CSV). Recorded as an assumption to verify with logging, not resolved
  at intake.
### Plan-stage Q&A (added by /skill:plan, session herdr-1793358530-3252013-3553)

- Q: "Is an endpoint-wide (slot-less) registry entry safe, or does it risk
  annotating live work and weakening the truthful contract?" — Answer (agent,
  code evidence + design): safe when the matcher requires that the processing
  slot has **no** lease owner and no live dispatch record; the negative case is
  pinned by a deterministic test before implementation
  (`LP-0MVUVHA55009EU4B`), and `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0 is unchanged in
  intent (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`). Source: `annotate_slots_for_status`
  already computes `owner_session_id`; `_build_slot_to_session_map` provides the
  dispatch-record binding.
- Q: "Should an endpoint-wide entry annotate a slot read from a *stale*
  `/slots` snapshot, and should a stale snapshot clear the entry?" — Answer
  (agent, design decision): annotate yes, clear **no**. The registry entry is
  fresh evidence about an abandonment, while `is_processing=false` is only
  trustworthy from a fresh snapshot; clearing on stale detail would let a
  cached "free" reading drop a live annotation, and the stale path is already
  reconciled by `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- Q: "Which key can represent 'endpoint-wide' without colliding with a real
  slot id?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): an `int` sentinel (`-1`) —
  llama-server slot ids in `/slots` and in `session._slot_owners` are
  non-negative, and the registry dict is typed `tuple[str, int]`, so a string
  sentinel would break the type contract. Recorded as a module constant so the
  assumption is explicit and testable.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show `local_abandoned_slots=0`?"
  — **OPEN QUESTION (carried forward, not resolved at plan time)**: not
  determinable from the 12-row artifact CSV. Routed to implementation child
  `LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK`, which adds `slot_source=` / `abandoned_slot_mismatch`
  diagnostics so the recorded vs observed slot id is answerable from production
  logs; the item's AC requires the answer be recorded (or a follow-on item
  created) before it closes.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent, confirmed at plan time): no — decomposed into follow-on child
  `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, mirroring `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the intake entry
  above remains the authoritative record. **Open to producer override.**

## Related work (automated report)

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want every queued local wait to record *how it
entered the queue* and *why it left without a slot*, so the abandoned-wait
share can be split by entry path and by cause instead of being a single
opaque 60.7 % — and so a full-budget expiry can never be confused with a
depth-cap refusal.

## Measured need (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Two entry paths feed one queue, and only one of them logs a reason:

| Path | Call site | Abandonments (post-change 24 h) | Logged reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_concurrency_limit` | `provider.py` first `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call | 89 / 314 (28.3 %) | **none** (the fallback line has no `reason=` field there) |
| `local_lease_active` retry | `provider.py` second `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call, after the local dispatch returned a `local_lease_active` 503 | 225 / 314 (71.7 %) | `reason=local_lease_active` |

Per-window split already derivable from the existing `reason=` field (own
measurement, same harness vocabulary):

| Window (24 h) | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | lease-active share | concurrency-limit share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` (pre) | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 41.7 % (20/48) | 23.5 % (4/17) |
| `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` (pre, diurnal) | 136 | 71 | 52.6 % | 53.3 % (57/107) | 50.0 % (14/28) |
| `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` (`52085f09`) | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 61.1 % (225/368) | 59.7 % (89/149) |

Also measured: **all** abandonments are full-budget expiries
(`queued_duration >= 55 s`; 314/314 post-change, 71/71 pre-change diurnal);
depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur, so the 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth`. That distinction is currently *inferred* from
the duration rather than logged.

## Scope

- Log `trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active` on both queue outcomes
  and on the enqueue line, and an explicit `cause=queue_wait_expired|
  queue_depth_exceeded` on both fallback call sites.
- Parse and report the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` in
  `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (the existing harness — do NOT
  create a second report; `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` owns the standalone
  contention-queue residual report).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: add `trigger=` + `cause=` to the two
  `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` and two `contention_queue_dispatch`
  log calls; derive `cause` from the returned action (`elapsed is None` with
  depth at cap → `queue_depth_exceeded`, otherwise `queue_wait_expired`) —
  never guess from the duration in the analyser.
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`: `_KV_TRIGGER`, `_KV_CAUSE`
  regexes; per-band and totals blocks gain `by_trigger` and `by_cause`
  counters; the markdown record renders the split.
- `tests/test_prefill_admission_conversion.py` + proxy tests: synthetic lines
  for both triggers and both causes; a legacy line without the new fields
  degrades to `unknown`, never dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Both fallback call sites log an explicit `cause=` (`queue_wait_expired` vs `queue_depth_exceeded`) and `trigger=` (`concurrency_limit` vs `local_lease_active`); the concurrency-limit site, which currently logs no reason at all, is attributable. Unit-tested from the provider call path.
- AC2: The enqueue line `contention_queue_wait` carries `trigger=` (and keeps `saturation=`), so an enqueue that never resolves is attributable.
- AC3: The harness reports the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` (totals and per band), and a synthetic-line test proves a depth-cap refusal (elapsed ≈ 0, `cause=queue_depth_exceeded`) is distinguished from a budget expiry (`cause=queue_wait_expired`) without inferring from duration.
- AC4: A log line lacking the new fields (pre-change shapes) is parsed as `unknown` and never dropped — asserted by a test using a pre-change line shape.
- AC5: Re-running both committed windows reports the split (expected: 0 depth refusals) with the numbers pasted from tool output, and the record's markdown shows it.
- AC6: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; guardrails `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) / `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) and the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering untouched.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`
- `tests/test_prefill_admission_conversion.py`
- `proxy/tests/` (queue + log-shape tests)

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: the band-attribution fix (own-request join) child.
- `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` — standalone sweep report owner (consumes these fields).
- `LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI` — the completed item that introduced the lease-active queue path.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the `local_lease_active` re-queue path to
honour the request's priority and to charge a request's queue budget **once per
turn**, so a `high`-priority request is never parked there and a request that
already waited cannot be handed a fresh 60 s.

## Defects found by code reading (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

`proxy/proxy/provider.py` has two `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites:

1. the `local_concurrency_limit` check — passes `priority=_priority`;
2. the `local_lease_active` retry (entered after the local dispatch returned a
   `local_lease_active` 503) — passes **no `priority=`**, so `priority=None`
   reaches both `_contention_queue_enabled(config, priority)` and
   `_prefill_admission_guard(..., priority=priority)`. The documented contract
   is that `high` priority **never queues**; on this path that contract is not
   enforced, and the guard pricing no longer knows the priority either.

Second defect: the lease-active path re-enters the queue **after** the request
already spent its wait (or none) at the concurrency gate, and nothing carries
the spend forward — `_contention_queue_remaining_seconds` is computed for the
*response* but the *next* `wait_for_local_slot` is called with the full
`max_wait_seconds`. A request can therefore accumulate up to two full budgets
in one turn, which inflates both the abandoned-wait denominator and the user's
latency (measured: 368 lease-active waits vs 143 dispatches in the post-change
24 h window, 61.1 % abandoned).

## Scope (bug fix, test-first)

- Pass the priority through on the lease-active call site.
- Carry the spent queue wait on the request and bound the second wait by the
  measured remainder, so cumulative queue wait never exceeds
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` for one turn.
- Keep the guardrails: no new knob, no change to the 60 s / 120 s values.

## Minimal implementation

- `provider.py`: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot(..., priority=_priority)` at the
  lease-active site; read/write the spent-wait marker through the existing
  `_set_queue_wait_on_request` / request attribute used by the deferral path,
  and pass `max_wait_seconds = min(cq_max, remainder)` (a keyword or a new
  helper argument on `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, defaulting to today's
  behaviour for callers that pass nothing).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`: optionally accept an already-spent
  duration so the waiter's own bookkeeping/`queued_duration` reflects the
  cumulative wait (no change to wake-up logic).
- Tests first: high-priority lease-active request does not queue
  (`fallback_policy`-equivalent, no `contention_queue_wait`); a request with a
  spent wait gets at most the remainder; an untouched path behaves
  byte-for-byte as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `local_lease_active` retry call site passes the request's priority, and a unit test asserts a `high`-priority request never waits in that queue (returns without a queue wait, matching the documented `high` never-queues contract).
- AC2: A request that already spent queue wait in the same turn is bounded by the measured remainder at the second wait, and a unit test asserts cumulative queue wait ≤ `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (no second full budget).
- AC3: `queued_duration` / the logged wait for the lease-active path reflects the cumulative wait for the turn (observable), and the `trigger=`/`cause=` fields from the observability sibling are populated on this path.
- AC4: Guardrails unchanged and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering test `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green; no new configuration knob.
- AC5: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing queue, deferral, reservation and lease tests pass unchanged in intent (any intent-preserving update is called out in the commit message).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py` (or the closest existing lease/queue suites)

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: trigger/cause observability.
- `LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C` — the completed item that made the lease denial queue.
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (holder-side capping) — NOT in scope here.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard (or the queue
admit criterion) to price the blocker class the diagnosis proves is holding the
slot — so a queue wait that cannot be served inside the 60 s budget is refused
up-front instead of burning the full budget and detouring remote — or, if the
diagnosis does not support a change, a committed decision that says so.

This is the behaviour-change slice. It is deliberately gated on the diagnosis
record so the change is driven by evidence, not by the assumption that the
guard is "too permissive".

## Context (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Measured in the post-change 24 h window: 314/517 enqueued waits abandoned, all
at the full budget; 225/314 were `reason=local_lease_active`; for the 176
abandonments with a session-level preceding guard decision, 170 were `admit`
with median `projected_wait_s = 35.8 s`. The guard's occupancy term prices peer
*prefill* service (including the re-priced occupant remaining new tokens from
`LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) but not the *generation* time of a lease holder that
keeps the slot after its prefill.

## Scope

- Extend the projected-wait quantity so the diagnosed blocker class is priced
  (for example, a lease/decode hold term raised into the existing occupancy
  maximum — evidence can only raise the floor, never lower it), and/or refuse
  a queue admit whose remaining budget cannot outlast the blocker.
- Preserve every documented invariant: measured evidence can only raise the
  symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor; fail-open on missing/invalid records;
  warm prompts unchanged; no new configuration knob; `high` priority never
  queues.
- Out of scope: capping the lease holder's consecutive renewals — that is
  `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.

## Minimal implementation

- Test first: simulated blockers in `proxy/tests/` — (a) a blocker whose
  remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining budget ⇒ refuse (or
  defer under the pin semantics), (b) a short-prefill blocker ⇒ admit exactly
  as today, (c) missing/invalid occupant record ⇒ fail-open (today's floor).
- Then the minimal guard change in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (plus the
  caller plumbing in `provider.py`/`router_helpers.py` if the blocker snapshot
  is not already available) and the log fields that make the new term
  attributable.
- Document the rollback using existing knobs only
  (`local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A unit test shows a blocker whose remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining queue budget causes a refusal (or the pin-semantics deferral) instead of a full-budget queue wait; a short-prefill blocker still admits with the same decision as today.
- AC2: The change only prices the blocker class named by the diagnosis, never lowers the symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor, and a test asserts fail-open on missing/invalid occupant evidence (no guessed multiplier).
- AC3: Guardrails untouched and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green, no new configuration knob, `high` priority never queues.
- AC4: Rollback is documented using existing knobs only, in `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`, and the page names this item and the diagnosis record as the evidence.
- AC5: The new decision term appears in the `local_admission_guard` log line (parsed by the usage report) so the post-fix window can attribute refusals to it.
- AC6: If the diagnosis does not justify a behaviour change, this item closes with a committed decision note instead of code, recording the measured rationale and re-scoping AC1-AC3 in a comment (no silent no-op).
- AC7: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py`, `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py`
- `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: abandoned-wait diagnosis, lease-active re-queue path fixes.
- `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ` — occupant-remaining re-pricing (the term being extended).
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (out of scope, linked evidence).

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a 24 h post-fix measurement of the
abandoned-queue-wait share, compared against the diurnally matched baseline and
the literal 85 % bar, so the regression item can be closed on evidence — or
kept open with numbers that say the fix did not work.

## Scheduling (learned from LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN)

- **Runnable at/after** (fix deploy timestamp + 24 h); the window end is fixed
  by the deploy of the behaviour-change sibling, not by "the last 24 h".
- **Do not run early.** A session starting before the window has elapsed stands
  down (claim nothing, edit nothing) and says so — a sub-24 h slice is not the
  record, and the 13 h slice taken on 2026-10-29 already showed a slice is not
  a substitute.
- Log retention: proxy logs rotate ~6 h with gzip retention back to
  `2026-10-15`; run within ~3 days of the window end.

## Scope

- Measure the fixed 24 h window with the fixed harness (own-request banding,
  trigger/cause split, contiguous-wait accounting) and the usage report.
- Compare against three references: literal 85 % bar; diurnally matched
  pre-change baseline (52.6 %); pre-fix post-change share (60.7 %).
- Count and explain `local_eviction_after_acceptance` by reason (no new class ⇒
  link a triage item if one appears).
- Update the operator docs and both records.

## Minimal implementation

- Commit `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postfix.md` + `.json` produced
  by the committed commands (no hand-typed numbers; the embedded command line
  regenerates the JSON).
- Update `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md` and
  `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` cross-references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The fixed 24 h window ending 24 h after the behaviour-change deploy is measured with the fixed harness and committed as `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postfix.{md,json}`, labelled with the deploy commit and both window bounds.
- AC2: The record reports the abandoned share against all three references (literal 85 % bar, diurnally matched pre-change 52.6 %, pre-fix post-change 60.7 %), split by trigger, cause and band, with per-hour rates alongside shares.
- AC3: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is counted by reason and compared with the previous windows; every class is zero or explained in one line, and any genuinely new class links to a triage work item.
- AC4: Every number is pasted from tool output and the embedded command regenerates the committed JSON byte-for-byte (modulo the rotation-dependent log-file inventory).
- AC5: A session that starts before the window has elapsed stands down without claiming or editing anything (asserted by the record's "window not yet elapsed" note when applicable), mirroring the LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN scheduling-hold pattern.
- AC6: `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md` and `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` are updated, and the closing verdict is recorded on parent `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR` (share met or not, with numbers).

data.description:
# Goal

Bring `slots_stale` under **5 %** of `/llama/local/status` polls (the measured target of
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 AC1) by making the `/slots` counts/detail refresh meet its handler budgets
under real load — or, if that is not achievable at the configured budgets, establish the evidence
and move the contract deliberately.

# Problem statement

The 24 h re-measurement of 2026-10-29 (window `2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00` local,
coverage `covered`, no gaps, 2 proxy restarts inside the window at 12:58:34 and 14:09:25) measured:

| Metric | 24 h value | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Status polls | 26,019 | — |
| `slots_stale=true` | **7,698 (29.59 %)** | < 5 % → **missed** |
| stale source | `detail_cache` 7,224 / `counts_cache` 474 / unknown 0 | — |
| stale-poll refresh latency | ≥5 s 2,063 · 2–5 s 3,888 · 1–2 s 1,637 · <1 s 110 | — |
| `capacity_hint` idle/prefill_bound/saturated/abandoned_busy | 16,160 / 6,156 / 3,293 / 410 | — |
| `saturated` with no live local work | 70 (0.27 % of polls) — 65 attributed, 5 unattributable | 0 |
| herdr downtime dispatches (durable trail) | 81 (target ≥ 10) | **met** |
| Local dispatches | 829 (143 sessions, 29 herdr; warm 576 / cold 253) | — |

Same-window trend of the metric on successive builds:

| Window | Build | `slots_stale` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 20:00 → 07:00 (night) | `56a3a28a`/`2d2b6b51` (router `/slots` path) | 79.61 % |
| 2026-10-28 09:30 → 21:30 (12 h) | child-port resolver `f58e8964` live | 53.92 % |
| 2026-10-29 01:00 → 2026-10-30 01:00 (24 h) | `f58e8964` live + later HEAD | **29.59 %** |

The child-port resolver removed the router from the polling path and roughly halved the stale rate,
but **77 % of the residual stale polls were served from cache after a refresh that took longer than
the 2 s counts / 1.0 s (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) detail budget**. Staleness is therefore no longer a
router artefact: the `/slots` read path still exceeds its budget under load, so `slots_stale` is
reporting real latency, not a truthfulness defect (the cache-time reconciliation of
LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM still holds — only 70 polls, 0.27 %, showed `saturated` without live work).

# Evidence and re-derivation

- Artifacts: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure/` (`measurement.json`,
  `measurement.txt`, `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, `prefill_thrash_skips.csv`,
  `SUMMARY.md`, `provenance.json`).
- Command (read-only, verified tool LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK):

  ```bash
  python3 scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py \
    --since '2026-10-29 01:00' --until '2026-10-30 01:00' --window-closed \
    --label 24h-remeasure --limit 250 --json \
    --write-artifacts ~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_24h-remeasure
  ```

- Durable herdr dispatch trail re-derived from `wl export` (`author=herdr-downtime` +
  `Auto-dispatched` + `createdAt` inside the window): 81 dispatches, 53 distinct items.

# Not in scope (tracked elsewhere)

- Router `/slots` HTTP 400 responses — LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 (this item is about latency/staleness,
  not 400s).
- Nightly report generator publishing `slots_stale` / `capacity_hint` — LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0.
- Abandoned-dispatch ghosts inflating `abandoned_busy` — LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB.

# Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `/slots` counts/detail read path is profiled under load and the dominant contributor to
  > 2 s refreshes is named with per-path timing evidence (child-port request concurrency, per-poll
  fan-out, llama-server `/slots` cost, or proxy-side serialisation).
- AC2: A 24 h window re-measured with the same tool shows `slots_stale < 5 %` of status polls;
  **or** the item records that the configured budgets cannot be met at peak load, with the measured
  latency distribution, and the producer decides whether to raise the budget or change the target.
- AC3: `capacity_hint=saturated` without live local work stays at 0, or every residual poll is
  attributed (the 24 h run left 5 unattributable out of 26,019).
- AC4: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` reflects the outcome, and the full suite is green.

## Related work

- discovered-from:LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (24 h re-measurement that measured this residual)
- Measurement items: LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ, LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV
- Fix that this residual survives: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (capacity truthfulness, unchanged)

# Plan (plan_complete, 2026-10-31)

Decomposition into three vertical phases, test-first. Effort/risk pre-check returned
`decision=plan` (Medium effort, Medium risk); the plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval=false`, so no approval pause was required.

## Evidence refresh (seed for this plan)

Live window 2026-10-31 00:42 → 04:52 local (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, current HEAD),
read-only analysis:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Status polls | 4,164 |
| `slots_stale=true` | 709 (17.03 %) |
| stale by poll latency | `< 1 s` 11 · `1–2 s` 172 · `2–5 s` 355 · `≥ 5 s` 181 |
| `slot_counts_stale=true` | 0 |
| `slots_detail_stale=true` | 657 |

So the residual is now **entirely the per-slot detail query**, and it is a real latency signal: the
handler awaits `query_llama_status()` (1 s budget) then counts (2 s) then detail
(`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`, 1 s) **in series**, and the detail fetch duplicates work the 1 s periodic
refresher already does (`_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at`). Idle child-port
`/slots` costs 0.7–5.5 ms, so the cost is load-dependent backend latency, not route cost.

## Phases and children

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Test: /slots read-path freshness contract (LP-0MVVXGHHB0073W1B) | task | — |
| F1 | Instrument per-phase /slots read-path timings (LP-0MVVXGHT1001I5YX) | task | T1 |
| F2 | Profile 24 h window; name dominant contributor (LP-0MVVXGI490089OX5) | task | F1 |
| F3 | Serve shared /slots snapshot on status path (LP-0MVVXGLTM008ROJ9) | feature | T1, F2 |
| F4 | slots_stale from snapshot age; schema 5 (LP-0MVVXGM54009TOXD) | feature | F3 |
| F5 | Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) | task | F3 |
| F6 | Re-measure 24 h window; record AC2 disposition (LP-0MVVXGMRN007NCJP) | task | F3, F4, F5 |
| F7 | Docs and full-suite green (LP-0MVVXGN2C004O28B) | docs | F6 |

### Phase A — evidence (T1 → F1 → F2)

Tracer bullet through code → `status_request` log → analysis tool → recorded evidence. Ends with the
dominant contributor named per parent AC1, and an explicit instruction that F3/F4 descriptions are
updated if the evidence contradicts the assumed fix.

### Phase B — fix (T1 → F3 → F4/F5)

Tracer bullet through the handler read path → payload/log → consumer contract → attribution. One
shared `/slots` snapshot; counts and detail derived from the same payload; `slots_stale` defined by
snapshot age rather than cache use; stale reconciliation preserved.

### Phase C — verdict (F6 → F7)

Re-measure a full ≥ 24 h window with the same tool and record either `slots_stale < 5 %` (AC2 first
branch) or the measured latency distribution and the producer decision request (AC2 second branch);
then documentation and full suite (AC4).

## Reused implementations (no new machinery where one exists)

- `_fetch_slots_payload()` — TTL caching + single-flight coalescing (LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT).
- `_last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at` — stamped shared snapshot.
- `_resolve_slot_details_for_enrichment()` — pristine-cache discipline (LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — `slots_stale_attribution.by_source` /
  `by_latency_band`, `--write-artifacts` (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK).
- `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint()` — cache-time reconciliation (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) stays the
  guard that makes snapshot-serving safe.

## Assumptions (documented, not invented requirements)

1. The measured residual is dominated by backend `/slots` latency under load plus per-poll fan-out;
   F2 is the gate that confirms or refutes this before F3 is implemented.
2. A snapshot age of ≤ 2 s (two refresher cycles) is an acceptable freshness budget for a
   dispatcher that polls at ~17 polls/min; the value is env-configurable and revisited in F6.
3. `slots_stale` redefined as age-over-budget is the honest observable; the alternative (keep
   "served from cache") makes the metric unmeasurable once the poll path serves a warm snapshot by
   design. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 in the Appendix, to be confirmed before F4.
4. The item is a `bug` with four ACs, so no epic-level feature splitting below the eight children.

## Duplicate-work check

`wl search slots_stale` / `/slots latency` / `single-flight slots` / `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`: no
completed item covers this scope. Nearest relatives and why they are not duplicates:
LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 (measurement, closed with a documented miss), LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ (detail-cache
fallback, delivered), LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y (single-flight cancellation, delivered),
LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (post-cancel release lag, different defect), LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB (abandoned-work
annotation, delivered).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-31 — initial decomposition: 8 children created (T1, F1–F7), 10 dependency edges wired,
  evidence refresh recorded, AC-section boundary fixed (`# Related work` → `## Related work` so the
  coverage review stops parsing provenance links as acceptance criteria). Stage → `plan_complete`.
